recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future CareTeam edits should preserve the current distinction between CareTeam assigned to a group and the Group resource itself, but FHIR-13338 needs no further core-source work.
issue_request: FHIR-13338 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 Patient Care change request asking the CareTeam introduction and scope text to make clear that CareTeam is not limited to a singular patient and can also apply to a group, with examples such as married-couple therapy or a support group; the resolution also noted subject-less organizational/event teams and dynamic team membership.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied in git commit bd3f8a7ba5aba2347a6542d772cdc96897766a9c, whose subject includes "#13338 Update CareTeam intro" and whose patch changed source/careteam/careteam-introduction.xml to mention a single patient, a group, subject-less organizational teams, and dynamic/transient team membership.
additional_context: CareTeam is an active current-build resource in source/fhir.ini. Later final CareTeam issues retained and refined the same model: FHIR-14760 clarified why CareTeam.subject can be omitted and why Group is a valid subject target; FHIR-20909 restructured the introduction into the current patient/group/event bullet list; and FHIR-28457 added subject guidance for when to use Group versus Patient. No directly relevant Zulip or Confluence record was found that conflicts with the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because the current CareTeam introduction and StructureDefinition already communicate the requested patient-or-group scope and the related subject-less event/team case.
